claim: The widget renders the escaped `**col:** value` text via renderTextBlock (markdown-it html:false, breaks:true), and the backslash escapes (including \< \& \|) come out as literal characters. The new comment above createMarkdownRenderer states this accurately.
verify_against: markdown-it backslash-escape rules (CommonMark ASCII punctuation escapes) and renderTextBlock
verify_hint: renderTextBlock/createMarkdownRenderer in query_results.html; CommonMark escape rules for & and |
evidence: renderTextBlock (query_results.html:772-785) builds markdownRenderer via createMarkdownRenderer(window.markdownit) which calls markdownit({ html: false, linkify: false, typographer: false, breaks: true }) at line 753, matching the claim. The comment block at lines 740-751 (inside md-renderer:start/end markers) accurately documents html:false as the XSS boundary, no images, validateLink default, and breaks:true for newlines. Server side, src/sqllens/tools/_format.py defines _SMALL_RESULT_ESCAPED_CHARS = frozenset("\\`*_[]<>~|&") (line 49) and _escape_small_result_text (line 1192-1197) backslash-escapes each of those characters, used to build '**col:** value' lines (line 1218). Per CommonMark's backslash-escape rule, any ASCII punctuation character (including & < > | which are all in the ASCII punctuation set) may be backslash-escaped and renders as the literal character rather than being interpreted as markup; markdown-it (a CommonMark-compliant parser) implements exactly this rule. Thus \<, \&, \| all render as literal <, &, | characters through renderTextBlock/createMarkdownRenderer as claimed.
